title: Baterías y vehículos por mar: lista de verificación P903/P912 bajo IMDG 42-24
summary: Guía en español para identificar la configuración real, verificar UN 38.3, confirmar la entrada IMDG y obtener aceptación escrita del transportista.
content:
🔋
Última verificación: 30 de julio de 2026. La edición 2024 del Código IMDG, incluida la Enmienda 42-24, es obligatoria desde el 1 de enero de 2026.

Respuesta corta: no seleccione P903 o P912 solo por la palabra “batería”. Primero identifique cómo se presenta la mercancía: celdas o baterías solas, baterías embaladas con/instaladas en equipos, o un vehículo propulsado por batería. Después, un especialista competente debe confirmar el número UN, la denominación oficial, las disposiciones especiales y la instrucción de embalaje aplicables al modelo real.

La OMI confirma la entrada en vigor obligatoria de la Enmienda 42-24. Código IMDG — OMI

Tres controles antes de solicitar espacio

  • Vincule cada modelo físico con su clasificación, resumen de pruebas UN 38.3 y ficha de seguridad.
  • No reutilice automáticamente una declaración de otro modelo, capacidad, química o configuración.
  • Obtenga aceptación escrita del transportista para el origen, transbordos, destino y fecha propuestos.

Matriz operativa P903 vs. P912

PreguntaP903 — enfoque típicoP912 — enfoque típico
Tipo de mercancíaCeldas/baterías y baterías embaladas con o contenidas en equipos, según la entrada aplicableVehículos propulsados por determinados tipos de batería bajo las nuevas entradas correspondientes
IdentificaciónQuímica, modelo, energía, masa y relación con el equipoVIN o identificación del vehículo, tipo de batería, condición y sistemas activos
Riesgo principalCortocircuito, movimiento, daño físico, activación accidental y embalaje incorrectoMovimiento del vehículo, activación, fuga, daño de batería y condición no declarada
EvidenciaUN 38.3, SDS, especificación, declaración DG y embalaje conformeIdentidad del vehículo, condición, batería, aceptación del transportista, estiba y aseguramiento
Decisión finalConfirmar contra la entrada exacta de la Lista de Mercancías PeligrosasConfirmar contra la entrada exacta y las condiciones de P912

Esta tabla orienta la preparación; no reemplaza el texto del Código IMDG ni una clasificación competente.

Paso 1: identificar la configuración real

Prepare una hoja por modelo con:

  • fabricante y denominación comercial;
  • número de modelo o VIN;
  • química de la batería;
  • capacidad nominal y masa;
  • si la batería viaja sola, con equipo, dentro de equipo o integrada en vehículo;
  • condición: nueva, usada, prototipo, dañada, defectuosa, retirada o para reciclaje;
  • accesorios peligrosos incluidos;
  • embalaje exterior, palé, caja, contenedor o método de estiba.

No declare mercancía dañada o defectuosa como producto normal. Requiere una evaluación separada.

Paso 2: verificar UN 38.3

El resumen de pruebas debe permitir relacionar el tipo de celda o batería con el fabricante, laboratorio, informe, fecha, descripción física y resultados. Una SDS genérica no sustituye el resumen de pruebas.

Compare el nombre del fabricante, modelo, masa, energía y descripción con la placa o documentación del producto. Si el proveedor cambió celdas, configuración, BMS o componentes que puedan afectar el tipo probado, detenga la reserva hasta obtener una revisión competente.

Paso 3: confirmar la entrada IMDG

La Resolución MSC.556(108) contiene las enmiendas adoptadas y establece que la clasificación corresponde al expedidor/remitente o a la autoridad competente cuando así se especifica. Resolución MSC.556(108)

No use por costumbre un número UN antiguo para un vehículo de litio. La Enmienda 42-24 incluye entradas más específicas para vehículos según la tecnología de batería. Confirme:

  1. número UN;
  2. denominación oficial de transporte;
  3. clase y etiqueta;
  4. disposiciones especiales;
  5. instrucción de embalaje;
  6. documentación;
  7. estiba, segregación y aceptación del buque.

Paso 4: preparar embalaje y aseguramiento

Para celdas, baterías y equipos, proteja terminales, evite cortocircuitos, inmovilice el contenido y use embalajes compatibles con la instrucción aplicable. Para vehículos, documente condición, sujeción, prevención de activación y cualquier instrucción del transportista.

Registre fotografías del embalaje, marcas, etiquetas, número de contenedor, sello y trincaje. La aprobación documental no compensa una carga mal asegurada.

Lista de liberación para embarque

Qué enviar a DDNZ

Envíe modelo, química, capacidad, resumen UN 38.3, SDS, dimensiones, peso, forma de presentación, fotografías, origen, destino y fecha de carga lista. DDNZ puede preparar una lista de brechas y solicitar aceptación al transportista; el expedidor y el profesional competente conservan la responsabilidad de la clasificación y declaración final.

title: Transpacific Freight from China: A U.S. Import Risk Checklist
summary: A practical checklist for HTS and Section 301 review, coast comparison, quote scope, cargo-ready cut-offs and demurrage/detention control.
content:
🇺🇸
Last verified: 30 July 2026. This guide removes unverified weekly rate claims and focuses on controls that apply to a real U.S.-bound booking.

The short answer: for China–United States ocean freight, the largest avoidable risks are often not the headline rate. They are wrong tariff classification, incomplete quote scope, cargo not ready for cut-off, and unmanaged destination free time.

Three actions before booking

  • Confirm the U.S. HTS subheading and current trade-remedy exposure for the exact product.
  • Compare US West Coast, East Coast and Gulf options on total delivered cost and inventory risk.
  • Name the person responsible for arrival notices, customs release, terminal pickup and empty return.

Check tariff exposure by exact HTS subheading

The U.S. Trade Representative's official Section 301 search identifies covered products and rates by 8- or 10-digit HTS subheading. USTR Section 301 search

Do not calculate duty using a supplier's broad six-digit code alone. Build a product file with material, function, model, technical description, country of origin and proposed U.S. classification. Have the importer or customs broker confirm:

  • base HTS duty;
  • Section 301 or other Chapter 99 measures;
  • product-specific exclusions, if any;
  • antidumping/countervailing duty risk;
  • agency requirements for the product;
  • marking and country-of-origin rules.

A low ocean rate cannot rescue a shipment with an incorrect landed-cost assumption.

Compare coasts on the same scope

FactorUSWC
Main-carriage profileShorter Pacific crossing for many China origins
Inland dependencyRail/truck to central and eastern markets
Operational testTerminal appointment, rail availability, chassis and inland capacity
Best decision metricDelivered cost + expected lead time + stockout cost + destination-charge exposure

Always compare quotations from the same origin pickup point to the same final delivery point. If one quote is port-to-port and another is door-to-door, it is not a route comparison.

Approve a complete quotation

Require the quotation to state:

  • origin and destination;
  • equipment and weight assumptions;
  • commodity and dangerous-goods status;
  • direct or transshipment service;
  • inclusions and exclusions;
  • rate validity and sailing window;
  • documentation and security charges;
  • destination terminal, drayage and rail components;
  • demurrage/detention free time;
  • cancellation, rollover and change terms.

If the supplier changes the ready date, weight, package count or commodity, obtain a revised confirmation.

Control demurrage and detention

The Federal Maritime Commission confirms that its detention and demurrage billing rule took full effect on 28 May 2024 and sets invoice-content requirements. Federal Maritime Commission

Operationally, prevent charges before relying on a dispute process:

  1. secure customs documents before arrival;
  2. monitor arrival notices and last free day;
  3. confirm terminal release and payment holds;
  4. pre-arrange chassis, appointment and truck;
  5. record pickup and empty-return attempts;
  6. keep screenshots and correspondence when appointments are unavailable;
  7. review invoices immediately.

The importer, customs broker, forwarder and trucker should share one arrival checklist with named owners.

Book only cargo that can meet cut-off

Request the factory's production and inspection schedule before booking. Use a warehouse closing date that allows time for:

  • final quality inspection;
  • document correction;
  • export packing;
  • consolidation;
  • verified gross mass;
  • shipping-instruction approval;
  • carrier cut-off and gate-in.

For seasonal goods, split critical inventory rather than rushing an entire order with incomplete data.

Shipment control sheet

MilestoneOwnerEvidence
Classification approvedImporter / brokerHTS decision and duty calculation
Cargo readySupplier / China teamInspection release and packing data
Booking confirmedForwarderCarrier/NVOCC confirmation and cut-offs
Loaded and gated inWarehouse / truckerContainer, seal, VGM and terminal record
Arrival clearedImporter / brokerCustoms and terminal release
Empty returnedTruckerReturn receipt and date

What to send DDNZ

Send the product description, proposed HTS, supplier city, Incoterm, cargo-ready date, cartons/pallets, weights, dimensions, destination postcode and inventory deadline. DDNZ can compare coastal routings and provide a booking/arrival control sheet. Live rates, tariff measures and space must be reconfirmed for the actual shipment.

Escalation triggers before departure

Pause the shipment if the confirmed HTS differs from the purchase documents, the cargo misses inspection, the carrier changes the routing, or destination free time is not stated. Assign one owner to resolve each exception and record the revised decision. A short written exception log prevents different parties from working from outdated booking, customs or delivery instructions.

  • FMC — detention and demurrage billing rule

title: China-Europe Railway Express: A Route-Selection Guide for Importers
summary: Choose a rail service by cargo origin, planned departure, border corridor, destination terminal, commodity acceptance and ICS2 readiness—not an unaudited route list.
content:
🚆
Last verified: 30 July 2026. This guide replaces an unaudited “193 routes” list with a route-selection method based on current official network data and shipment-level confirmation.

The short answer: choose a China-Europe rail service by cargo-ready location, scheduled departure, border corridor, destination terminal, EU customs-data readiness and last-mile delivery—not by the nearest Chinese station or an online transit-time table.

Current network context

Official China State Railway Group reporting in May 2026 described:

  • 129 Chinese cities operating China-Europe Railway Express services;
  • 235 connected cities in 26 European countries;
  • more than 100 connected cities in 11 Asian nations;
  • 93 scheduled lines designed for 120 km/h operation.

These figures show network breadth, not availability for every commodity or week. State Council Information Office of China

Five route-selection questions

  1. Where is the cargo actually ready?
  2. Which terminal has a confirmed departure for the required destination?
  3. Which border corridor and transshipment plan will be used?
  4. Is the commodity accepted across every country on the route?
  5. Who files EU safety/security and transit data and arranges final delivery?

Route decision matrix

FactorEvidence to requestReject the quote if
Origin terminalPickup plan, warehouse closing date and planned trainOnly a city name is provided
Border corridorNamed exit/entry points and transshipment methodThe route is “flexible” without change-control terms
DestinationActual rail terminal, customs location and last-mile planThe quote says “Europe” without a terminal
Transit estimateTerminal-to-terminal scope, planned departure and bufferThe number is presented as guaranteed without service conditions
CommodityWritten acceptance for weight, batteries, liquids, temperature or oversizeAcceptance is assumed from a generic cargo description
Customs dataExporter, transit, ENS and destination-filing responsibilitiesNo party is named for house-level data

Origin-terminal choice

The closest station is not always the best option. Compare the domestic truck distance and cost against departure frequency, cut-off discipline, consolidation capability and destination coverage.

For Pearl River Delta suppliers, a service from a nearby South China hub may reduce domestic handling. For mixed suppliers in eastern and central China, a more distant consolidation hub may offer a better planned departure. The decision must be based on the shipment date and destination, not a permanent ranking of cities.

Border and corridor risk

Cross-border rail involves changes of rail gauge, customs/transit procedures and multiple railway operators. Ask for the intended corridor and what happens if it changes. A rerouting can affect transit documents, sanctions screening, insurance and destination delivery.

For cargo to Central Asia, confirm whether the service ends at the destination country or continues under a separate road/rail handoff. For EU cargo, identify the first EU entry point and the party responsible for security and transit filings.

ICS2 for rail arrivals

The European Commission requires accurate and complete pre-arrival Entry Summary Declaration data for rail and road cargo under ICS2. European Commission — road and rail ICS2

Provide a precise goods description, parties, package count, weight, transport document references and HS information at the required level. If several suppliers are consolidated, the house-level data must remain traceable.

Rail, ocean or air?

ModeTypical roleDo not use when
RailHigher-value, time-sensitive Eurasian cargo with suitable inland terminalsCommodity or corridor acceptance is uncertain
OceanHigh-volume cargo with more flexible lead timeStockout cost is greater than the time saving of a faster mode
AirSmall, urgent or production-stopping quantitiesChargeable weight makes the product uneconomic

A split shipment is often stronger than choosing one mode for every line item.

Data pack for a firm rail request

Send:

  • supplier pickup addresses;
  • cargo-ready date;
  • product description and HS proposal;
  • cartons, pallets, gross weight and volume;
  • lithium battery or dangerous-goods information;
  • export and destination parties;
  • destination rail terminal or postcode;
  • Incoterm and customs arrangement;
  • maximum acceptable delivery window.

Ask for a written route, service scope, validity, cut-offs, commodity acceptance, planned departure and contingency.

What to send DDNZ

DDNZ can compare origin terminals, confirm candidate corridors, build an ocean-versus-rail landed-cost sheet and identify ICS2 data gaps. The final booking remains subject to space, commodity acceptance, route controls and current customs requirements.

title: Exporting Pure Electric Passenger Vehicles from China in 2026: Licence, DG and Destination Gates
summary: A verified gate-by-gate guide separating China's new pure-EV passenger export licence from carrier dangerous-goods acceptance and destination vehicle approval.
content:
🚗
Last verified: 30 July 2026. This article replaces an unsupported project case study and separates three approvals that are often confused: China export licence, dangerous-goods transport acceptance and destination-market vehicle approval.

The short answer: from 1 January 2026, China applies export-licence administration to the specified pure-electric passenger vehicles described in MOFCOM Announcement No. 54 of 2025, with reference customs code 8703801090. This is not the same as IMDG acceptance or permission to register the vehicle in the destination country.

Three independent gates

GateResponsible decisionWhat it does not prove
China export licenceEligible exporter and licence process under Chinese rulesCarrier acceptance or destination registration
Transport acceptanceCorrect vehicle/battery classification, condition, documents and stowage for the selected modeRoadworthiness or market approval after arrival
Destination approvalHomologation, safety, conformity, import and registration requirements in the buyer's marketThat the Chinese exporter is licensed

Do not release payment or move vehicles to port until all three gates have named owners.

1. Confirm whether the 2026 licence rule applies

MOFCOM, MIIT, GACC and SAMR announced export-licence administration for “other passenger vehicles equipped only with a drive motor and having a vehicle identification code,” with reference customs code 8703801090, effective 1 January 2026. MOFCOM Announcement No. 54 of 2025

For each shipment, confirm:

  • new or used vehicle status;
  • vehicle type and intended customs classification;
  • VIN and model;
  • exporter named on the declaration;
  • manufacturer's and exporter's eligibility;
  • export licence number and validity;
  • consistency across contract, invoice, vehicle certificate and customs data.

The official 2026 application notice describes the online process and reiterates that planned exporters of the covered pure-electric passenger vehicles must apply as required. MOFCOM 2026 application notice

2. Freeze a VIN-level commercial file

Create a master vehicle list before transport:

  • VIN;
  • manufacturer, brand and model;
  • production date and condition;
  • battery chemistry, model and rated energy;
  • colour and configuration;
  • unit value and Incoterm;
  • export certificate/licence references;
  • destination-market approval reference;
  • keys, accessories and spare parts;
  • photographs of VIN, nameplate, exterior and odometer where applicable.

Any change after booking should trigger document revalidation.

3. Prepare transport acceptance

The 2024 IMDG Code edition including Amendment 42-24 is mandatory from 1 January 2026. Vehicle classification depends on battery technology, condition and how the vehicle is presented for transport. IMO IMDG Code

Before requesting Ro-Ro, container or rail space, send the carrier:

  • vehicle model and VIN quantity;
  • battery type and transport classification;
  • UN 38.3 evidence for the battery type where applicable;
  • SDS or safety information requested by the carrier;
  • vehicle condition and state-of-charge information where required;
  • dimensions, weight and ground clearance;
  • leak, alarm, immobilisation and key-control status;
  • destination and transshipment route.

Used, damaged, defective, accident-involved or recalled vehicles require separate disclosure and may not be accepted on a standard service.

4. Choose Ro-Ro or container by the shipment

FactorRo-RoContainer
Typical fitOperational vehicles on a supported port pairSmall lots, special routing or added physical enclosure
HandlingPort driving, key control and vehicle condition reportLoading geometry, blocking/bracing and container weight distribution
Main riskPort acceptance, sailing schedule and vehicle accessImproper securing, tight clearances and hidden damage
EvidenceVIN list, condition photos, acceptance and handover recordVIN list, loading plan, securing photos, container and seal record

For either mode, obtain written carrier acceptance for the actual model and condition.

5. Destination-country gate

Ask the importer or homologation adviser to confirm before purchase:

  • whether the model may be imported and registered;
  • required safety and conformity approvals;
  • steering side, lighting, charging interface and language rules;
  • battery or environmental requirements;
  • age or condition restrictions for used vehicles;
  • duties, taxes and valuation;
  • after-sales, recall and spare-parts obligations.

A vehicle that can leave China may still be commercially unusable at destination.

Release checklist

What to send DDNZ

Send the VIN/model list, new/used status, exporter, reference HS code, licence status, battery data, dimensions, origin, destination and preferred mode. DDNZ can prepare a gate-by-gate document checklist and request carrier acceptance. Final export, DG and destination approvals remain with the responsible licensed parties.

title: دليل سابر 2026 للاستيراد من الصين: الرمز الجمركي وشهادة المنتج والإرسالية
summary: مسار عملي موثق لتحديد رمز التعرفة السعودي من 12 رقماً، نطاق اللائحة، شهادة المنتج وشهادة الإرسالية قبل شحن البضاعة من الصين.
content:
🇸🇦
آخر تحقق: 30 يوليو 2026. تم حذف ادعاءات الغرامات والعروض البحرية غير الموثقة. هذه قائمة تشغيل عملية مبنية على سابر وهيئة الزكاة والضريبة والجمارك.

الخلاصة: لا تبدأ الشحن من الصين قبل ربط كل موديل برمز جمركي سعودي مكوّن من 12 رقماً، وتحديد ما إذا كان المنتج خاضعاً للائحة فنية، وإكمال مسار شهادة مطابقة المنتج أو الإقرار المطلوب، ثم إصدار شهادة الإرسالية ببيانات الفاتورة والشحنة نفسها.

ثلاث خطوات حاسمة

  • صنّف المنتج في التعرفة المتكاملة السعودية، ولا تعتمد على رمز عام يقدمه المصنع.
  • سجّل كل موديل في سابر بالمسار الصحيح: منتج منظم أو غير منظم.
  • طابق بيانات سابر والفاتورة وقائمة التعبئة وبوليصة الشحن قبل مغادرة البضاعة الصين.

توضح منصة سابر الرسمية أنها تدير تسجيل المنتجات وشهادات المطابقة وشهادات الإرسالية للمنتجات الاستهلاكية الداخلة إلى السوق السعودي. منصة سابر

مسار الامتثال من المنتج إلى الإرسالية

المرحلةالسؤال المطلوبدليل الإغلاق
التصنيفما الرمز السعودي المكوّن من 12 رقماً؟تأكيد المستورد أو المخلص وربطه بالموديل
نطاق اللائحةهل المنتج خاضع للائحة فنية؟نتيجة البحث في سابر واللائحة ذات الصلة
مطابقة المنتجهل يلزم PCoC أم إقرار للمستورد؟شهادة/إقرار صالح يغطي المصنع والموديل
مطابقة الإرساليةهل بيانات الفاتورة والكمية وبلد الشحن متطابقة؟شهادة إرسالية صادرة للشحنة الفعلية
التخليصهل تطابق الجمارك بين الرمز والمستورد والشهادات؟ملف موحد لدى المستورد والمخلص والوكيل الصيني

1. ابدأ بالرمز الجمركي الصحيح

تذكر هيئة الزكاة والضريبة والجمارك أن التعرفة المتكاملة لدول مجلس التعاون تُطبّق على مستوى 12 رقماً، وتنشر البنود المستحدثة والمحذوفة والتعديلات. التعرفة الجمركية المتكاملة

أرسل للمخلص قبل طلب الشراء:

  • وصف المنتج ووظيفته؛
  • المادة الأساسية؛
  • صور المنتج واللوحة الفنية؛
  • رقم الموديل؛
  • الجهد والتردد والطاقة للأجهزة؛
  • طريقة الاستخدام: منزلي أو تجاري أو صناعي؛
  • الملحقات والمواد الملامسة للغذاء إن وجدت.

قد يؤدي تغيير الموديل أو الوظيفة أو المادة إلى تغيير التصنيف أو متطلبات المطابقة.

2. حدّد اللائحة الفنية للموديل

لا يكفي أن يقول المورد إن لديه “SASO”. افحص ما إذا كانت الشهادة تغطي:

  • اسم المصنع نفسه؛
  • الموديل نفسه؛
  • بلد المنشأ؛
  • اللائحة والمواصفة الحالية؛
  • جهة تقويم مطابقة مقبولة؛
  • مدة صلاحية الشهادة.

بالنسبة لمعدات المطابخ التجارية والثلاجات والأجهزة الكهربائية، قد تتقاطع متطلبات السلامة الكهربائية وكفاءة الطاقة ومواد ملامسة الغذاء والبيانات الإيضاحية. يجب تحديد المسار حسب المنتج الفعلي.

3. افصل شهادة المنتج عن شهادة الإرسالية

توضح سابر أن شهادة مطابقة المنتج تثبت مطابقة المنتج للوائح ذات العلاقة، بينما تصدر شهادة مطابقة الإرسالية بعد اكتمال مسار المنتج أو الإقرار للمنتج غير الخاضع.

بيانات الإرسالية يجب أن تعكس الشحنة الحقيقية:

  • رقم وتاريخ الفاتورة؛
  • المستورد؛
  • المورد أو المصنع؛
  • الموديلات والكميات؛
  • قيمة ووحدة المنتجات؛
  • بلد الشحن؛
  • بيانات بوليصة الشحن عند الطلب.

لا تستخدم شهادة إرسالية قديمة لشحنة جديدة.

4. راجع الملف في الصين قبل التحميل

أنشئ جدولاً رئيسياً يربط كل سطر في أمر الشراء بما يلي:

  1. موديل المصنع؛
  2. الرمز الجمركي السعودي؛
  3. اللائحة الفنية؛
  4. رقم شهادة المنتج أو الإقرار؛
  5. الكمية في الفاتورة؛
  6. عدد الطرود والوزن؛
  7. العلامات والبيانات على المنتج والكرتون.

أثناء الفحص قبل الشحن، صوّر اللوحة الفنية والملصق ورقم الموديل والعلامات العربية المطلوبة. قارن الصور بالملف الفني.

5. لا تعتبر DDP بديلاً عن الامتثال

مصطلح DDP يوزع التكاليف والمسؤوليات التجارية، لكنه لا يجعل منتجاً غير مطابق مقبولاً. يجب تحديد المستورد النظامي، صاحب حساب سابر، جهة التخليص، الضرائب والشهادات في العقد. اطلب تفصيلاً مكتوباً للتكاليف والاستثناءات بدلاً من عرض “شامل” غير محدد.

قائمة الإفراج قبل الشحن

ما الذي ترسله إلى DDNZ؟

أرسل قائمة المنتجات والموديلات والصور والمواصفات والمصانع والكميات والوجهة والمستورد السعودي وموعد الجاهزية. يمكن لـ DDNZ إعداد جدول فجوات سابر ومراجعة اتساق مستندات الشحن؛ يبقى قرار التصنيف والمطابقة النهائي لدى المستورد والجهات المختصة.

نقاط يجب حسمها مع المصنع قبل دفع الرصيد

اطلب من المصنع تأكيداً مكتوباً يربط كل موديل بالصور واللوحة الفنية ومواد التصنيع والجهد والتردد والملحقات. لا تقبل ملفاً فنياً عاماً لعدة موديلات مختلفة. إذا تغير مكوّن أو وظيفة أو اسم موديل بعد إصدار الشهادة، أوقف التحميل حتى يؤكد المستورد وجهة المطابقة أن التغطية ما زالت صحيحة. احتفظ بنسخة مؤرخة من المواصفات والفاتورة النهائية ونتيجة الفحص، وحدد شخصاً مسؤولاً عن أي اختلاف بين مستندات المصنع وسابر.

title: Importer de Chine vers l’Afrique francophone : contrôle documentaire et consolidation
summary: Guide pratique fondé sur les procédures officielles du Maroc et du Sénégal pour préparer les documents, consolider les fournisseurs et comparer le coût porte-à-porte.
content:
🌍
Dernière vérification : 30 juillet 2026. Ce guide remplace les anciennes promotions de fret et les pourcentages non vérifiables par des procédures officielles au Maroc et au Sénégal.

Réponse courte : pour importer depuis la Chine vers l’Afrique francophone, verrouillez d’abord le pays d’importation, le code SH, le titre ou l’autorisation d’importation, les documents produit et le déclarant en douane. Ensuite seulement, consolidez les fournisseurs et comparez le fret sur une base porte-à-porte.

Trois règles simples

  • Une procédure marocaine ne doit pas être copiée pour le Sénégal, l’Algérie ou la Côte d’Ivoire.
  • Le devis fournisseur n’est pas un dossier douanier : description, valeur, origine et exigences produit doivent être confirmées par l’importateur.
  • La consolidation réduit parfois le transport, mais elle augmente le risque documentaire si les produits et fournisseurs ne restent pas traçables.

Maroc : préparer le titre d’importation dans PortNet

PortNet explique que le titre d’importation est la première formalité : une marchandise libre à l’importation exige un engagement d’importation, tandis qu’une marchandise soumise à autorisation exige une licence d’importation traitée dans la plateforme. PortNet Maroc

Avant la production, le client marocain et son transitaire doivent confirmer :

  • le statut libre ou autorisé de la marchandise ;
  • le code SH marocain ;
  • la domiciliation ou les formalités financières applicables ;
  • les contrôles techniques ou sanitaires ;
  • les documents à téléverser ;
  • le port et le bureau de dédouanement.

Le fournisseur chinois doit recevoir une description et un modèle déjà validés, pas seulement le nom commercial utilisé dans le catalogue.

Sénégal : constituer le dossier et nommer le déclarant

Les Douanes sénégalaises indiquent que les marchandises importées doivent faire l’objet d’une déclaration et que l’importateur recourt normalement à un commissionnaire en douane agréé. Elles listent notamment la facture commerciale, le document de transport, le certificat d’origine, l’assurance et les certificats spécifiques au produit. Douanes sénégalaises

Le dossier exact dépend de la marchandise et de la valeur. Demandez au commissionnaire de confirmer par écrit :

  • la déclaration préalable ou le contrôle requis ;
  • les documents produit ;
  • la base de valeur en douane ;
  • les droits et taxes estimés ;
  • la procédure portuaire et d’enlèvement ;
  • le délai de remise des originaux.

Matrice documentaire avant expédition

DocumentContrôle en ChineValidation à destination
Facture commercialeVendeur, acheteur, modèle, quantité, prix, devise, IncotermValeur, classement et partie importatrice
Liste de colisageColis, poids net/brut, dimensions et marquesCorrespondance avec la déclaration et l’inspection
ClassificationDescription technique et proposition de codeCode SH final confirmé par l’importateur/déclarant
OrigineFabricant réel et éléments d’origineCertificat et traitement tarifaire, le cas échéant
Conformité produitModèle, rapports, étiquettes et photosAutorisation, norme, contrôle ou certificat national
TransportRéservation, connaissement, conteneur et scelléAvis d’arrivée, mainlevée, livraison et retour du conteneur

Consolider plusieurs fournisseurs sans perdre la traçabilité

Créez une ligne de contrôle par bon de commande :

  • fournisseur légal et adresse ;
  • référence interne et modèle ;
  • nombre de cartons ;
  • poids et volume ;
  • code SH proposé ;
  • exigence de conformité ;
  • résultat d’inspection ;
  • emplacement dans l’entrepôt et dans le conteneur.

Étiquetez chaque carton avec une référence lisible. Photographiez la marchandise, les plaques signalétiques, les emballages et le chargement. Après consolidation, la liste de colisage maître doit se réconcilier avec les documents de chaque fournisseur.

Comparer le fret correctement

Ne choisissez pas un port ou un service parce qu’une ancienne publication annonçait une promotion. Demandez un devis daté et valable pour votre cargaison réelle.

Comparez :

  1. enlèvement chez les fournisseurs ;
  2. entrepôt et consolidation ;
  3. manutention et formalités en Chine ;
  4. fret principal ;
  5. frais portuaires à destination ;
  6. dédouanement ;
  7. surestaries et détention ;
  8. livraison finale ;
  9. assurance ;
  10. taxes et droits séparés.

La solution la moins chère au départ peut coûter davantage si elle ajoute un transbordement, une livraison intérieure longue ou peu de jours de franchise.

Contrôle produit avant paiement final

Pour les équipements de cuisine, réfrigérateurs, machines, appareils électriques ou articles en contact avec les aliments, inspectez le modèle réel : tension, fréquence, prise, plaques, matériaux, fonctions, pièces de rechange, emballage et étiquetage. Le certificat doit couvrir le fabricant et le modèle expédiés.

Ce qu’il faut envoyer à DDNZ

Envoyez le pays et l’adresse de destination, la liste des produits, les modèles, les villes fournisseurs, les quantités, les poids/volumes, l’Incoterm, le code SH proposé et la date de disponibilité. DDNZ peut établir un plan de consolidation, une comparaison logistique et une liste d’écarts documentaires. L’importateur et son déclarant national confirment les décisions douanières finales.

title: China–Saudi Freight Before September 2026: Check Gateway, Cargo Acceptance and Surcharges Before Booking
summary: Before booking China–Saudi cargo, compare current Saudi gateway acceptance, cargo-type restrictions, landbridge routing and carrier-specific surcharges—not one headline freight rate.
content:
China–Saudi cargo moving into September 2026 cannot be booked responsibly from one headline ocean-freight number. Maersk introduced a Peak Season Surcharge of USD 1,000 for all 20-foot containers and USD 2,000 for all 40/45-foot containers from Far East Asia to Saudi Arabia, effective 10 August. But the more important question is whether the carrier will accept your exact cargo through your intended Saudi gateway. Current carrier notices differ by cargo type, port and routing. Before paying a deposit, tie the quote to the cargo, gateway, confirmed route, surcharge validity and fallback plan.

Three points for Saudi importers

  • Confirm cargo acceptance before comparing price. Dry, reefer, dangerous-goods and out-of-gauge bookings may not have the same Saudi gateway options.
  • Treat the port and inland point as separate decisions. A quote to Dammam may involve discharge at Jeddah and a landbridge rather than a direct ocean call.
  • Ask for an itemised, dated quote. Base ocean freight, PSS, emergency or contingency charges, inland transfer, destination charges and free time should not be hidden inside one total.

What changed in the current market

Maersk’s PSS notice applies from China and other Far East Asian origins to Saudi Arabia from 10 August 2026 until further notice. The notice also says other local and contingency charges may apply. That means an importer should not assume the PSS is the only addition to the base rate.

The operational side is even more important. In its 19 August Middle East update, Maersk published different booking positions for Jeddah, King Abdullah Port, Dammam and Jubail, with further differences for dry, reefer, dangerous-goods, in-gauge and out-of-gauge cargo. The notice is carrier-specific and volatile; it is not a permanent rule for every shipping line.

A gateway-and-cargo check before requesting rates

Shipment scenarioPublic notice to investigateWhat the buyer should obtain in writing
Dry cargo to Jeddah or King Abdullah PortMaersk listed acceptance on 19 August, subject to availabilityConfirmed port of discharge, vessel or service, space status and quote validity
Dry cargo for Dammam or JubailMaersk’s 19 August notice described dry-cargo restrictions at Dammam/Jubail and continued Saudi movements through Jeddah; Hapag-Lloyd’s 17 August update said Dammam had no delays but required case-by-case planningOcean port, landbridge provider, place of delivery, inland cost and estimated handover sequence
Reefer cargo for Dammam, Jubail or King Abdullah PortMaersk listed suspension for these gateways in the 19 August noticeCarrier-specific alternative, temperature responsibility, plug-in/storage exposure and a live acceptance reference

Out-of-gauge cargoMaersk listed broad Saudi suspensions in the same noticeDo not rely on a standard online quote; request case approval and an alternative routing study

This table is a starting point, not a booking confirmation. The booking must match the carrier notice that is live on the day of acceptance.

Why carrier schedules are not interchangeable

Two current independent carrier notices show why a generic “Saudi rate” is unreliable. MSC announced on 24 August that selected East–West Suez transits would resume service by service. It also stated that booking confirmations and online schedules would be updated progressively and that contingency changes remained possible.

Hapag-Lloyd’s Week 34 Middle East update, last updated 17 August, reported no delays at Dammam but said operations still required case-by-case planning. It also reported pressure at Jeddah, including high yard density and full reefer capacity at the time of the update.

The practical conclusion is simple: a route shown on a schedule page is not the same as an accepted booking for your commodity, container and delivery point.

Make every forwarder quote comparable

Send the same RFQ sheet to every forwarder. It should state:

  1. Chinese origin city and intended loading port.
  2. Saudi final delivery city, not only a preferred seaport.
  3. Commodity, HS code if known, cargo type and any temperature or dangerous-goods condition.
  4. Container size, gross weight, volume and cargo-ready date.
  5. Required service: port-to-port, port-to-door or door-to-door.
  6. Separate lines for base ocean freight, PSS, emergency/contingency charges, origin fees, landbridge or feeder cost, destination fees and inland delivery.
  7. Quote validity, free time, routing, transshipment points and what happens if the planned gateway stops accepting the cargo.
  8. The booking reference or written carrier acceptance needed before the supplier releases cargo.

A lower rate with an unconfirmed gateway can become the most expensive option after rerouting, storage or inland transfer. For Saudi importers, dealers and project contractors, the useful quote is not the shortest number. It is the quote whose route, cargo acceptance, cost lines and contingency responsibility can all be checked.

title: What Saudi Coffee-Equipment Dealers Should Source from China Before September 2026
summary: A practical guide for Saudi dealers choosing compact, café and automatic coffee equipment from China—without overloading the range or overlooking service.
content:
When Saudi dealers compare coffee equipment from China, the biggest catalogue is rarely the best starting point. A dealer needs a range the sales team can explain, the technician can install and the buyer can reorder. For most distributors, that means three clear choices: a compact machine for small counters, a two-group machine for busy cafés and an automatic option for hotels or self-service locations. The goal is not to collect more models. It is to choose a few that suit local customers, arrive with the right documents and can be supported after the sale.

✅
In brief
  • Start with three clear customer needs instead of dozens of similar machines.
  • Compare the complete package, not the machine price alone.
  • Test a small first order before expanding the range.

Why the timing matters

CoffeeZone is scheduled for 15–17 September 2026 in Riyadh, bringing together hospitality buyers, equipment suppliers, roasters and café operators.

For a dealer, the useful work happens before the event: decide which customer segments matter, prepare a short list and know what questions to ask. Three well-understood packages will start better conversations than twenty machines with little more than a photo and a price.

Build a range customers can understand

1. Compact bar package. This works for small cafés, bakery counters and restaurants where space is tight. A sensible package includes a single-group machine, a properly matched grinder, water treatment and basic bar tools. Compact should mean a smaller footprint—not domestic-duty equipment sold as commercial.

2. Standard café package. A two-group semi-automatic machine suits busier cafés that make espresso and milk drinks at the same time. Ask for the electrical load, water and drainage needs, dimensions and a short list of essential spare parts. These details tell the installer far more than the word “commercial” on a product page.

3. Hotel or self-service package. Bean-to-cup machines can work well for breakfast areas, offices and convenience locations. Here, cleaning, milk storage, waste water, menu setup and access to the grinder matter as much as cup output.

Two price positions, two different buyers

The photographs show why price only makes sense when it is tied to a customer and a complete package.

Premium reference: above USD 20,000

The lever-operated setup in the photograph retails above USD 20,000. It belongs in a premium conversation where design, theatre, finish and the complete bar setup matter. Before offering it, make sure the quote clearly states the machine, grinder, accessories, training, warranty and spare parts included.

Mid-tier reference: around USD 6,000

The automatic machine shown in several views sits around USD 6,000. It may suit buyers who want a distinctive product without moving into the premium price band. Dealers should still compare the exact model, accessories and after-sales package.

For a fair margin comparison, put both offers on the same basis: trade terms, freight, tax, installation and warranty.

What to check before you quote a model

Use this table when comparing suppliers. If an answer is missing, get it before showing the machine to a customer.

QuestionWhat to ask forWhy it matters
Who will use it?Outlet type, menu, busy-period workflow and operator skillKeeps a light-duty machine out of a demanding café
Which machine will arrive?Model code, revision, selected options and nameplate photoMakes the production unit easier to match with the approved sample
Will it fit the site?Power, water, drainage, ventilation, dimensions and service clearanceLets the contractor prepare the counter before delivery
Can it handle the rush?A test using the intended drinks, grinder, water and cleaning routineShows how the machine behaves in the dealer's real sales scenario
Can we service it?Parts list, manuals, fault codes, training and first-order sparesAvoids waiting for every small part to arrive from China
Can we import and reorder it?Saudi documents, packing data, lead time and model-change policySupports a repeatable offer instead of a one-off sample

What Chinese specification sheets can—and cannot—tell you

A good specification sheet helps a dealer understand the installation before the machine reaches Saudi Arabia. Dr. Coffee, for example, publishes voltage, power, dimensions, water pressure and service-clearance information for its F2 platform. Jiangsu Amalfi lists boiler sizes, dimensions and weight for its CM500-2, while Huazell separates compact single-group machines from larger multi-boiler models.

The point is not which brand wins. It is whether every shortlisted machine comes with enough information for the dealer, installer and technician to make the same decision.

Check the Saudi import route before ordering

Saudi importers can use the Saber platform for product and shipment conformity services, while SASO lists coffee makers within its IECEE national recognition system. The exact route depends on the product classification and model. IEC 60335-2-75:2024 is a useful technical reference for commercial dispensing appliances, but the Saudi importer should check the final model and documents before shipment.

The machine is only half the offer

A dealer's reputation is tested after the sale, when a technician needs a part or a customer reports a fault. Ask the supplier:

  • which parts are shared across the range;
  • whether manuals and wiring diagrams match the shipped machine;
  • which spare parts should be stocked locally;
  • how warranty parts and model changes are handled;
  • what happens to branding, territory and direct customer enquiries.

These points may not look exciting in a showroom, but they decide whether the second order is easier than the first.

Start small and learn from the first order

Choose one model for each customer group you genuinely serve. Check the specification, inspect the sample and test it with the grinder, water and drinks your customers will use. Photograph the nameplate, internal layout, accessories and packing so the production order can be checked against the same reference.

If the sales team cannot explain the differences or the technician cannot support the machine, do not add more models yet.

Ask DDNZ to compare a dealer-ready shortlist

If you are a Saudi importer, coffee-equipment dealer or café-project contractor, send DDNZ the customers you sell to, target retail price, destination city and expected first order. We can compare suitable China-based suppliers, show what each quotation includes and identify which machines need more technical work before you present them to buyers.

title: Insulated Cooler Boxes for African Distributors: Compare Ice Retention, Payload and Container Cost
summary: A low cooler-box quote is not comparable until the supplier discloses the ice-retention method, usable payload, packed CBM and hardware specification. Use this buyer matrix before ordering from China.
content:
Direct answer

An African distributor buying insulated cooler boxes from China should not compare quotations by unit price or “days of ice” alone. First make every supplier test the exact offered model under the same ambient profile, starting temperatures, ice-to-payload ratio, opening cycle and temperature endpoint. Then compare verified usable payload, empty and loaded weight, export-carton CBM, container quantity and replaceable hardware. Without those controls, a cheaper box may carry less saleable product, lose cooling performance sooner in real heat, occupy more container space or generate costly latch, hinge and gasket returns.

Estimated reading time: 6 minutes

Three-point summary

  • A retention claim is not comparable without a method. “Four days” at 25°C indoors with a box full of ice is not the same result as four days in a hotter route with beverages, repeated openings and a defined temperature limit.
  • Catalogue litres do not show distributor margin. Verify internal usable dimensions, ice-to-payload ratio, carton cube and actual units per container.
  • Lock the exact model before payment. Approve a golden sample, bill of materials, gasket and hardware specification, test sheet, carton and replacement-parts list.

Why this category deserves attention in 2026

Current signals show activity at both the premium-brand and distribution ends of the cooler market. YETI reported that its global Coolers & Equipment sales increased 11% in the first quarter of 2026, while a Sub-Saharan African distributor announced a regional YETI rollout through wholesale and retail channels. These are company-level signals, not proof of continent-wide demand or a forecast for every price segment. They do show why African wholesalers should define their intended resale tier before asking China suppliers for the lowest price (YETI Q1 2026 results; LUKS Group distribution announcement).

A box for low-price beverage resale, a rugged fishing cooler and a premium outdoor-lifestyle product are different commercial offers. The quote should state the target user, payload, route, selling price band and expected warranty support before construction and accessories are compared.

“Four days of ice” is not one test

The active ASTM D3103-20(2025) method for thermally insulated distribution packages explains that performance depends on the actual package, external temperatures, energy source, coolant and product payload. It recommends testing the real package where possible, or using a simulation that closely matches the real payload and coolant (ASTM D3103).

The current WHO cold-box methodology makes the same comparability principle visible: for its specialised vaccine boxes, cold life has a defined ambient temperature, payload system and endpoint. WHO measures one class at a constant 43°C until the warmest storage point reaches 10°C. That is a medical cold-box protocol, not a consumer-cooler certification and not a claim DDNZ applies to ordinary outdoor boxes. It is useful here only because it shows what a defined test looks like (WHO E004).

Supplier pages reviewed on 14 August 2026 illustrate the problem. One China supplier states 4–6 days at 25°C indoors with the cooler fully packed with ice, and also publishes internal dimensions and carton CBM. Another brochure states four days, while a third product page states more than 60 hours; the reviewed pages did not disclose the same ambient, payload ratio, opening cycle and endpoint. These are seller statements, not independently verified results (Boright 33QT; Cool Ride brochure; Polymer 16QT).

Cooler claim comparison and buyer test matrix

Use one written protocol for every shortlisted sample. Choose the ambient profile from the intended market and route instead of copying a universal temperature.

Test fieldRequired supplier entryWhy it changes the result
Exact sampleModel, mould revision, materials, insulation and net weightPrevents a tested sample being replaced by a cheaper production version
PreconditioningStarting temperature of box, ice/coolant and payloadA pre-chilled empty box can overstate real-use performance
Ambient profileTemperature and humidity over timeIndoor 25°C and a hot delivery route are not equivalent
PayloadProduct type, mass/volume and starting temperatureWarm beverages or food consume cooling capacity
Ice/coolant ratioMass and arrangement of ice or packs versus payload“Full of ice” leaves less saleable payload
Opening cycleNumber, duration and timing of lid openingsRetail and delivery use introduces hot air repeatedly
SensorsLocation, logging interval and calibration recordOne sensor can miss the warmest area or a poor lid seal
EndpointAgreed internal temperature or ice-loss criterion“Some ice remains” and “payload stays below target” answer different questions
RepeatsNumber of samples and runs; pass/fail toleranceOne favourable sample does not show production consistency
ReportTime-stamped data, photos, sample ID and exceptionsAllows the buyer to trace the result to the ordered model

A factory demonstration can screen samples, but it should not be presented as an independent laboratory certificate. If the intended use is food, pharmaceuticals or another controlled cold chain, the importer must separately confirm destination requirements and the applicable validation route.

Compare usable payload and container economics

A large catalogue capacity can hide thick walls, a tapered interior, wheel wells or a bulky lid. A useful specification separates external dimensions, internal top and bottom dimensions, empty weight and the capacity basis. For example, YETI’s current size guide publishes both internal and external dimensions and states can capacity at a 2:1 ice-to-can ratio. That is a disclosure benchmark, not a recommendation to copy its construction or performance (YETI hard-cooler size guide).

Ask each China supplier for:

  • verified internal dimensions at the narrowest usable points;
  • payload capacity at the agreed ice/coolant ratio;
  • net and gross unit weight;
  • individual carton dimensions and gross weight;
  • pallet or floor-loading plan;
  • verified units per 20GP, 40GP and 40HQ;
  • whether boxes can nest without damaging gaskets or surfaces;
  • spare-parts cartons and their added cube.

Two calculations expose a misleading low quote:

Landed cost per usable litre = landed unit cost ÷ verified saleable-payload litres

Container margin before overhead = sellable units × expected unit margin − sample, inspection, spare-parts, damage, finance and freight allowances

Customs duties and taxes must be calculated for the exact destination and product classification. Do not reuse one country’s landed-cost assumption across West, North and Southern Africa.

Inspect the parts that create returns

Rotomoulded, injection-moulded and blow-moulded boxes can each serve a price tier; the manufacturing process alone does not prove quality. The buyer should verify wall and insulation consistency, lid alignment, gasket compression, latch force, hinge-pin retention, handle anchors, drain leakage, wheel attachment where fitted, colour consistency and odour.

Before the deposit becomes non-refundable, require a sealed golden sample and an approved specification sheet. Before shipment, compare production units with that sample, weigh a sample across cartons, repeat the agreed thermal screen, operate latches and hinges repeatedly, leak-test drains, inspect carton protection and confirm spare gaskets, latches, hinges and drain plugs. The purchase order should prohibit unapproved material, mould or component substitution.

RFQ handoff for a China sourcing plan

Send DDNZ the supplier quotations, model links, target countries, expected resale tier, order quantity, payload, required cooling duration and destination port. DDNZ can organise a comparable RFQ, supplier-document review, sample test plan, inspection scope, container-loading check and China export coordination.

title: Flete China–América Latina: el PSS baja al oeste y sube al este
summary: Los avisos de agosto muestran un PSS menor en algunas rutas hacia la costa oeste de América Latina y uno mayor hacia la costa este. Compare la ruta completa, no una sola tarifa regional.
content:
América Latina no se está moviendo como un solo mercado de fletes en agosto de 2026. Maersk redujo el recargo de temporada alta (PSS) en ciertas rutas desde Extremo Oriente hacia México, la costa oeste de Sudamérica, Centroamérica y el Caribe, pero lo aumentó hacia la costa este de Sudamérica. Al mismo tiempo, Buenaventura avanzaba en su recuperación tras el terremoto, aunque persistían limitaciones aduaneras y terrestres. Por eso, un importador debe comparar cada costa, puerto y fecha de carga por separado. Los importes siguientes son recargos, no cotizaciones completas de flete marítimo.

Tres datos que debe revisar un importador

  • Una reducción del PSS en una ruta hacia la costa oeste no significa que todos los embarques a América Latina sean más baratos.
  • La costa este de Sudamérica mostró la señal contraria en agosto, con países y fechas efectivas claramente definidos.
  • La operación del puerto, la aduana, la escala del buque y el transporte terrestre pueden pesar más que el recargo en el costo y el plazo final.

Una región, dos direcciones para el PSS

Para fechas de cálculo desde el 3 de agosto, Maersk indicó un PSS de USD 750 por contenedor seco de 20 pies y USD 1.500 por contenedor seco de 40 pies desde Extremo Oriente hacia México, la costa oeste de Sudamérica, Centroamérica y el Caribe. En un aviso separado, el movimiento fue opuesto para la costa este desde el 20 de agosto: USD 1.000 por contenedor seco de 20 pies y USD 2.000 por contenedor seco de 40 pies hacia Argentina, Brasil, Paraguay y Uruguay. Aviso para la costa oeste; aviso para la costa este.

Grupo de rutasSeñal publicadaFecha efectivaQué debe hacer el importador
México / costa oeste de Sudamérica / Centroamérica / CaribePSS Maersk: USD 750 / 20 pies; USD 1.500 / 40 pies3 ago 2026Volver a cotizar el par de puertos exacto; no descontar el PSS de una tarifa anterior sin confirmación
Costa este: Argentina / Brasil / Paraguay / UruguayPSS Maersk: USD 1.000 / 20 pies; USD 2.000 / 40 pies20 ago 2026Separar ofertas anteriores y posteriores a la fecha efectiva y confirmar la fecha de cálculo
Colombia / BuenaventuraRecuperación operativa con restricciones aduaneras y terrestresActualización: 14 ago 2026Comprobar terminal, escala e itinerario terrestre antes de prometer una fecha de entrega

CMA CGM también anunció un PSS de USD 1.000 por contenedor desde Asia hacia la costa este de Sudamérica para fechas de cálculo desde el 20 de junio y hasta nuevo aviso. Los avisos de ambas navieras no son intercambiables, pero confirman que la costa este debe analizarse como un corredor distinto. Aviso de CMA CGM.

Por qué esta diferencia afecta a importadores y distribuidores

Los agentes de importación, distribuidores y proveedores de proyectos suelen vender con un margen limitado y una fecha de entrega comprometida. Pedir una sola “tarifa para América Latina” oculta variables que pueden consumir ambos: terminal de origen, puerto de destino, tamaño del contenedor, transbordo, días libres, cargos locales y fecha utilizada para calcular el flete. El PSS puede cambiar mientras la tarifa base y otros recargos se mueven de forma independiente.

La comparación útil no es “¿qué aviso parece más barato?”, sino “¿qué ruta completa funciona para esta carga y esta fecha?”. La cotización debe separar el flete marítimo base, el PSS y los demás recargos; indicar qué gastos están incluidos en destino; y explicar la vigencia y la fecha de cálculo. Así se evita convertir un ajuste visible en una supuesta reducción garantizada del costo puesto en destino.

Buenaventura: la recuperación no eliminó todos los riesgos

El aviso de Maersk del 11 de agosto registró operaciones suspendidas, una operación de buque incompleta, una escala omitida y carreteras afectadas tras el terremoto en Colombia. El seguimiento del 14 de agosto informó puertas de importación limitadas, depósitos reabiertos y una escala prevista, pero todavía había restricciones en procesos físicos de aduana y en parte de la red terrestre. Actualización inicial; actualización de recuperación.

Que una terminal vuelva a operar no significa que cada escala, trámite aduanero o entrega terrestre haya regresado a la normalidad. Una nota independiente del 14 de agosto también señaló alteraciones meteorológicas, blank sailings y omisiones de escala en servicios Asia–América Latina. Conviene verificar el itinerario real antes de comprometer una llegada. Nota de RS Logistics.

La información que debe acompañar una solicitud de flete

  1. Puerto de origen en China, puerto de destino en América Latina y cualquier alternativa aceptable.
  2. Tipo de contenedor, descripción de la mercancía, peso bruto, condición de mercancía peligrosa y fecha de carga lista.
  3. Flete marítimo base, PSS, otros recargos, gastos de origen y gastos de destino mostrados por separado.
  4. Fecha de cálculo, vigencia, días libres, transbordo y riesgo conocido de blank sailing u omisión de escala.
  5. Para entregas puerta a puerta, disponibilidad aduanera y acceso terrestre hasta el destino final.

DDNZ puede comparar la estructura de rutas y cotizaciones cuando recibe esos datos. El objetivo no es prometer la tarifa más baja, sino mostrar qué costos están cambiando, qué supuestos operativos necesitan confirmación y qué opción permite al importador cotizar a su propio cliente con una base más clara.

title: Evergreen’s China–South Africa SAF Service: Should You Switch?
summary: Evergreen’s new weekly SAF service adds a real China–Durban/Cape Town option. Compare the route against terminal conditions, inland handover and total cost before switching.
content:
🚢
Direct answer: Evergreen’s new Far East–South Africa Express (SAF) gives China shippers a genuine additional weekly option to Durban and Cape Town. A July launch report documented its first Durban call, and later terminal records showed continuing Evergreen operations. That makes it worth quoting for South Africa-bound cargo, especially shipments from Shanghai, Ningbo and Shekou. It does not make a routing decision automatic. The published port-to-port transit must be checked against the actual origin cut-off, Durban or Cape Town terminal status, free-time terms and any inland handover. Use the new service as a competing route, then choose on shipment-level execution rather than the launch headline.

Three points to know

  • The launch moved beyond a press announcement. Freight News documented Ever Useful at the 3 July launch call, while a later DGT record listed Evergreen vessel Ever Utile working at Durban; the DGT sheet does not identify the service code.
  • The network adds a useful direct-call option. Published rotation information covers Shanghai, Ningbo, Kaohsiung, Shekou and Singapore before Durban and Cape Town.
  • Port execution still controls the final result. Durban Gateway Terminal is publishing live stack, storage and berth updates and has temporary import-stack rules in force through 31 August 2026.

What the SAF service changes

Freight News reported that the weekly SAF rotation calls Shanghai, Ningbo, Kaohsiung, Shekou, Singapore, Durban and Cape Town. It cited 27 days from Shanghai to Durban and 32 days from Shanghai to Cape Town, plus through-bill coverage to Gaborone and Harare. Those figures are useful for a first comparison, but they are carrier-published schedule values—not a promise for every shipment.

The operational evidence matters. Durban Gateway Terminal’s 25 July vessel update listed Ever Utile working under a Durban vessel visit, and the terminal’s live update page continued to publish vessel, stack, storage and berth records through 2 August. The launch report therefore supports the initial SAF call; the later DGT sheet separately confirms continued Evergreen terminal activity but does not label the SAF service code.

Decision fieldWhat SAF may improveWhat still needs confirmation
China originDirect rotation from major Central and South China portsExact CY cut-off, equipment release and rolled-cargo policy for the booked sailing
South Africa gatewayCalls at both Durban and Cape TownWhich gateway gives the better final-mile route for the consignee
TransitPublished weekly schedule and port-to-port benchmarkActual vessel schedule, berth window and delivery appointment
Inland reachThrough-bill options reported for Gaborone and HarareCarrier liability point, border handover, free time and final delivery scope
Total costExtra capacity can create a competitive quotationOrigin charges, destination charges, detention, storage and inland costs

Why a faster port-to-port number can still lose

A direct call removes some transshipment exposure, but it does not remove origin or destination variability. A sailing with a better headline transit can still produce a later delivery if the container misses the China cut-off, waits for a terminal appointment or cannot move inland within free time.

Durban Gateway Terminal’s 1 July notice temporarily extended general import stack periods from three to four days for vessels arriving between 1 July and 31 August 2026. The terminal said the measure supports cargo flow during seasonal volume, weather risk and a Navis system upgrade. It also stated that the arrangement is not extra storage capacity and excludes reefer and IMDG containers, whose rules remain different. Importers should therefore treat free-time and collection planning as separate commercial checks.

A five-step route decision

  1. Compare the same shipment. Ask competing forwarders to quote the same container type, gross weight, origin factory, destination and delivery scope.
  2. Verify the sailing. Record vessel/voyage, CY cut-off, estimated departure, estimated arrival and whether the quoted leg is direct.
  3. Check the live terminal page. Review current berth, stack and import-storage notices shortly before booking and again before arrival.
  4. Price the handover. Separate ocean freight from destination terminal charges, customs handover, truck or rail, border movements and possible waiting time.
  5. Set an exception plan. Agree who monitors delay, who can switch a delivery slot and when storage or detention exposure must be escalated.
i
Book SAF when its confirmed sailing, total landed logistics cost and inland handover are better for the actual shipment. Do not switch only because the route is new or because a published transit looks shorter.

What to send for a comparable freight quote

Send the origin postcode, cargo description, HS code if available, package count, dimensions, gross weight, ready date, container requirement, destination address and any dangerous-goods or temperature-control condition. Ask the quote to show validity, included charges, excluded charges, free time and the named route or service.
